precision: f32 operations; uint8 router embeddings preserved; TF32 disabled
protocol: Two alternating rounds, one engine per process, 1,000 timings per run, 20 warm-ups, all 100 reference cases checked first. Same named input tensors; concurrency 1; four model CPU threads. Native accelerators add one dedicated control thread. Profiling stops before timing. Warm filesystem caches.

build.reduced: ORT v1.28.0 source da9b5e364c465de65c49d91e696cd6485270757f; MinSizeRel; basic minimal; reduced operators/types; shared library; no RTTI/ML ops. Exact command retained. System Protobuf 34.1 and Abseil 20260107.1 are included in the inventory.

coverage.ort_cuda_router: CPU shape/index partitions plus CUDA tensor computation; profile retains per-provider operator and copy counts.
coverage.native_cuda_router: All dense encoder/head GEMMs on CUDA; attention, norms, RoPE, embeddings, activation, residuals, and biases on CPU.
coverage.ort_cuda_mnist: All eight optimized compute nodes per inference on CUDA; host I/O copies can occur outside profiled graph nodes.
coverage.native_cuda_mnist: Three GEMMs on CUDA; im2col, bias/ReLU, pooling, and preparation on CPU.
coverage.native_potion_accelerator: Unsupported; explicit requests fail. CPU comparisons retained.
coverage.apple: Native CPU library cross-check passed for aarch64-apple-darwin. Accelerator cross-check needs the Apple SDK; no device results. NEEDS_OWNER.md records qualification.
coverage.mobile: Assessment only; no iOS/Android app or device package is qualified.

caveats: Shared host; other work was not stopped. Raw records include observed system load. Our own builds finished before the final timing runs.
These router runs cycle all 100 reference inputs, including long sequences. They are not the earlier route-v1 CPU workload.
Latency excludes preprocessing and HTTP; memory is process RSS with models live, not GPU peak memory. GPU VRAM peak was not sampled.
Eager CUDA loading can increase startup time and GPU memory; load latency and process memory remain in raw records.
Native accelerator implementations use mixed CPU/GPU execution; CPU fallback is reported true. No whole-graph native GPU claim.

The reduced CPU runtime passes all references but is slower here. Its 2.42 MB library also needs the Protobuf/Abseil closure; use the complete 10.88 MB executable-plus-library inventory for comparison.

Package inventories are uncompressed benchmark executables, shared libraries, and model assets. System prerequisites are separate; these are not final mobile app sizes or redistributable release archives.
Dual-engine inventories keep both representations of the weights. Native-only deployed loaders do not need source ONNX or test archives.

Minimal ORT-format tensor execution uses the generic adapter and exported graphs. High-level ORT model loaders still use original ONNX and full ORT. Conversion/source caches stay outside the deployed minimal payload.

Fixed x86 CPU ORT graphs and this reduced library do not establish ARM, CUDA, Core ML, or arbitrary-model coverage. Minimal ORT emits an expected unsupported Model Editor API diagnostic; tensor inference succeeds.
mobile_assessment: Ship only the model families an app needs. Native CPU avoids ORT. iOS Core ML/Metal need an Apple SDK, target-specific signed framework/app integration, and real-device parity, startup, memory, and thermal measurements; Android needs target ABI libraries and libc++ dependencies. Do not reuse fixed x86 ORT exports for those targets.
